title: What Is Boxing Day? Why the Day After Christmas Is a Holiday In Some Parts of the World
summary: Boxing Day falls on Dec 26. Learn its origins, where it's celebrated, and why some 2026 calendars show it on Dec 28.
body_markdown:
***Quick answer:** Boxing Day is a holiday on December 26, the day after Christmas. It began in Britain and is also observed in countries including Canada, Australia, and New Zealand. The name is commonly linked to charitable giving and gifts known as “Christmas boxes.” Today, Boxing Day is also associated with post-Christmas sales and sporting events. In 2026, December 26 falls on a Saturday, so some countries observe the public holiday on Monday, December 28.*


**Why is a Canadian retailer advertising a Boxing Day sale while an English soccer fan is talking about Boxing Day fixtures on the same calendar date? Both are referring to the same holiday, even though it looks completely different depending on where you live.**


**Boxing Day started in Britain as a tradition of giving. Over time, it grew into something broader: a public holiday observed across several countries, each with its own customs attached to it. For US readers who have only encountered Boxing Day through a Canadian sale ad, a British soccer match, or a conversation with friends and family abroad, the holiday can feel a little unclear. This guide breaks down what Boxing Day actually is, when it falls in 2026, why it has that name, and how different countries celebrate it today.**


## When Is Boxing Day in 2026?


Boxing Day falls on December 26 every year, the day immediately following Christmas. In 2026, that date lands on a Saturday.


Here’s where it gets slightly more complicated for anyone trying to plan around the holiday: when December 26 falls on a weekend, several countries use “substitute” public holidays to make sure workers still get a holiday on a weekday. A bank holiday is simply the British term for what Americans would call a public holiday, a day when banks, government offices, and many businesses close.


The table below outlines what to expect in four countries that recognize Boxing Day in 2026.


**Country** **What to know in 2026**


United Kingdom Monday, December 28 is the substitute bank holiday, according to GOV.UK.


Canada Boxing Day is December 26. Paid holiday status and substitute-day rules depend on the province or whether the employer is federally regulated.


Australia December 26 is Boxing Day. Check your state or territory calendar for the additional holiday on December 28 and local naming conventions, according to the Fair Work Ombudsman.


New Zealand The holiday is observed on December 26 or Monday, December 28, depending on an employee’s usual work schedule, according to Employment New Zealand.


If you’re coordinating with colleagues, family, or business partners in any of these countries, it’s worth double-checking the specific date they’ll have off, since it may not be December 26 itself.


## Why Is It Called Boxing Day?


The name “Boxing Day” has nothing to do with the sport of boxing. Its origin is generally traced back to two related traditions of giving around Christmastime.


The first involves households giving “Christmas boxes,” containing money or small gifts, to servants, workers, and tradespeople as a thank-you for their service throughout the year. The second tradition involves churches opening alms boxes, collection boxes used to gather donations throughout the year, and distributing the contents to people in need.


Both explanations are commonly cited as possible origins, and neither is treated as the single definitive source. What connects them is a shared theme: giving to others the day after Christmas. National Geographic generally traces the name to these Christmas gift boxes or church collection boxes rather than to any single, confirmed origin story.


## How Do People Celebrate Boxing Day Today?


Boxing Day traditions vary significantly by country, and understanding a few local customs can help explain why the holiday looks so different depending on where you encounter it.


### England and Holiday Soccer


In England, Boxing Day is closely associated with professional soccer. A fixture is simply a scheduled match, the term used throughout British sports to describe a game on the calendar. The Premier League has a long history of scheduling festive fixtures around Boxing Day, making it one of the busiest and most anticipated days on the English soccer calendar. For many fans, attending or watching a Boxing Day match is as much a part of the holiday as any other tradition.


### Australia and the Boxing Day Test


In Australia, Boxing Day marks the start of the Boxing Day Test, a major fixture in the cricket calendar. A Test match is a form of international cricket that can last up to five days, distinguishing it from shorter formats of the sport. In 2026, Australia is scheduled to play New Zealand at the Melbourne Cricket Ground, with the match starting on December 26.


### Canada and Boxing Week Sales


In Canada, Boxing Day has become closely tied to retail. Shoppers expect significant discounts on December 26, and many retailers extend the sales period into what’s known as “Boxing Week.” For US readers, the closest comparison is Black Friday: a single shopping day that has, for many retailers, grown into a longer stretch of promotional sales.


## Frequently Asked Questions About Boxing Day


### Is Boxing Day a federal holiday in the US?


No. Boxing Day does not appear on the US federal holiday calendar, according to OPM (the US Office of Personnel Management).


### Why do some calendars show Boxing Day on December 28 in 2026?


December 26, 2026 falls on a Saturday. In the UK, the substitute bank holiday is Monday, December 28, according to GOV.UK. Other countries, such as New Zealand, apply similar substitute-day rules depending on an employee’s regular work schedule.


### Does Boxing Day have anything to do with boxing the sport?


No. The name is generally traced to Christmas gift boxes given to workers and tradespeople, or to church collection boxes distributed to people in need, according to National Geographic.


## Understanding a Holiday That Travels Well


**Boxing Day began with a simple idea: giving to the people who supported you throughout the year. That spirit of generosity still underlies the holiday, even as its traditions have grown to include soccer fixtures in England, Test cricket in Australia, and retail sales across Canada.**


**Boxing Day serves as a reminder that holidays don’t always translate neatly across borders. The same date can mean a cricket match, a shopping trip, or a day off work with pay, depending on where you are. If you have family, friends, or business connections abroad, understanding these differences can help you plan ahead and avoid confusion around dates and expectations.**
